title: Genesis' two lights matched to the cosmic microwave background

tellings.quote: light returned to the universe and that's the light of the second day.

plain: Greg Rogers, described as a NASA doctor and a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, reads the opening of Genesis, the first book of the Bible, against modern science. He says the two separate lights in Genesis match the history of the early universe, from the faint glow left over from the Big Bang, which scientists call the cosmic microwave background, to the moment "light returned to the universe," which he calls "the light of the second day" when the first stars formed. If he is right, the ancient text would be describing the universe's beginnings accurately.
